CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 N. Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Room 280A
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Public Works Commission Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Friday, January 27, 2023
  11:00 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  January 27, 2023 / 11:00 AM

IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Julian Gold MD, Councilmember Sharona Nazarian PYSD,
  Public Works Commission Chairperson Wendy Nystrom, Public Works
  Commissioner John Millan, Public Works Director Shana Epstein, Utilities
  General Manager Robert Welch, Assistant City Manager Ryan Gohlich,
  Finance Director Jeff Muir, Senior Management Analyst Melissa Gomez,
  Executive Assistant Ilene Knebel, Rick Simonson (HF&H Consultants
  LLC)

1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Members of the public will be given the opportunity to directly address the Committee on any item
  listed on the agenda.

  Speakers:  None

2. RESOLUTION OF THE BEVERLY HILLS CITY COUNCIL LIAISON / RECREATION
  AND PARKS COMMISSION COMMITTEE AUTHORIZING PUBLIC MEETINGS TO BE
  HELD VIA TELECONFERENCING PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION
  54953(e) AND MAKING FINDINGS DETERMINATION REGARDING THE SAME.

  Comment: Recent legislation was adopted allowing the Beverly Hills City Council
  Liaison/Public Works Commission Committee to continue virtual meetings during the COVID-
  19 declared emergency subject to certain conditions and the proposed resolution implements
  the necessary requirements.

  Motion by Vice Mayor Gold. Seconded by Councilmember Nazarian.

3. STATUS UPDATE FOR THE WATER AND WASTEWATER COST OF SERVICE STUDY

  Public Works Director Shana Epstein introduced HF&H Consultant Rick Simonson, who
  presented information on the status update for the water cost of service study. He explained
  water revenue requirements with CIP options and other current capital projects, the water
  fund balance, cost of service (COS) allocations, proposed 2023 water COS rates and tier
  sizes for inside City and outside City customers, and the bill impacts for single family
  households, multi-family units, and businesses – the COS rates for single family households
  would increase in Tiers 1 and 2 but decrease in Tiers 3 and 4, while the rates for multi-family
  units and businesses would increase. Rate increases are needed, as costs will begin to
   outpace revenue by FY 2025-2026. Without rate increases, the city’s total water reserves
  would also begin to decrease in FY 2026-2027 beyond the City’s policy of maintaining a
  reserve target of 50% of operations and maintenance (O&M) . Continuing the outside city
  rate differential, pass-through rate adjustments, water reliability charge, and water shortage
  revenue stabilization factors practices were recommended.

  Commissioner Millan expressed hope for adding water projects to improve storage without
  them becoming a budget problem. Councilmember Nazarian shared that City Council is
  searching for further options for new wells. She said that the revised plan presented was
  more palatable, and asked if profit can be made from the cost of revenue services. Consultant
  Simonson said no, and the rate increases are needed to cover service and treatment costs.
  Councilmember Nazarian asked why other cities had lower water bills in comparison to
  Beverly Hills. Consultant Simonson explained that direct comparisons are difficult without
  exact knowledge of each city. Director Epstein gave examples of the different bill costs with
  Santa Monica, which is living off of funds from a successful lawsuit over contaminated water,
  and Ventura which is running off of local water only, which has its own benefits and
  drawbacks. Councilmember Nazarian expressed she would be in favor of the plan presented.
  Vice Mayor Gold expressed the importance of the issues of storage and costs to maintain
  water independence from Metropolitan Water District of Southern California (MWD).He asked
  how the city could sell the realignment and increased costs for single-family customers in
  Tier 1 and Tier 2 to promote water conservation and why Tiers 3 and 4 had lower rates.
  Consultant Simonson explained that Tier 1 is expanded which would allow single-family
  customers to stay in the lowest Tier for longer. He also explained that water rates cannot be
  solely based on water conservation due to rate setting regulations in California. Vice Mayor
  Gold said he believed that the new rates would be sellable, but his only real concern is how
  the city can incentivize citizens to use less water. Consultant Simonson said that education
  to the public is essential.

  Chairperson Nystrom and Vice Mayor Gold expressed concern that those single-family
  customers in Tier 3 and Tier 4 might see the new rates as a discount when they are the
  highest water users. Vice Mayor Gold asked if we can impose penalties for excessive usage.
  Director Epstein said that the City is currently imposing fines for customers violating water
  conservation rules. Director Epstein explained that Tier 4 was shrunk and tier sizes are under
  review. She also said that fines are much more influential, as they are public record and can
  be printed in newspapers. Vice Mayor Gold asked if the liaison could come back to another
  meeting with an established excessive water use policy to change the optics and encourage
  water conservation, expressing concern that the media would run with headlines about
  Beverly Hills lowering their water rates for higher water users. Director Epstein explained that
  the rates being shown to the liaison would only be in effect for the first six months, before the
  next rate increase, which takes effect January 1, 2024. Vice Mayor Gold asked for a plan to
  encourage conservation for everyone especially high water users, and steps to encourage
  water conservation. Chairperson Nystrom commented that the public would only look at the
  first year of rates. Commissioner Millan commented that the City is being proactive and
  responsible by maintaining the treatment plant, pursuing additional wells and storage, and
  promoting water conservation as the City cannot be fully reliable to MWD. Vice Mayor Gold
  closed the meeting by saying they would schedule a meeting to discuss wastewater rates
  sometime soon.

ADJOURNMENT
Date / Time:  January 27, 2023 / 12:00 PM
